tags.notable_features: U-shaped horseshoe bay, anchor chains from whaling era, resident frogfish, multiple moray eel species including dragon eel, finger reef wall structures both sides of bay
tags.marine_life: Hawaiian green sea turtles (honu), dragon moray eels, snowflake moray, frogfish (resident), octopus, leaf scorpionfish, devil scorpionfish, hermit crabs, cone snails, spotted eagle rays (rare), Galapagos sharks (rare), Hawaiian monk seals (occasional), trumpet fish, triggerfish

tags.notable_features: Three partial lava tubes with archways and overhangs; site is located a few hundred yards offshore in front of the former Sheraton Kauai Resort; sandwiched between Koloa Landing to the west and Ice Box to the east
tags.marine_life: Hawaiian green sea turtles (consistently encountered, often 10+ per dive), whitemouth moray eels, tropical reef fish, octopuses, nudibranchs, white-tip reef sharks (occasional), manta rays (rare seasonal)
tags.depth_note: Depth range reported 20-70 feet (6-21m) by Garden Isle Divers/Fathom Five; Seasport Divers' current listing (re-checked 2026-08-07) states 35-70ft for the low end -- sources not fully consistent on shallow limit

tags.notable_features: Horseshoe inlet with remains of steam schooner Pele (sank March 24, 1895 after striking sunken rock Kalanipuao); wreck remains include boiler, hull plates, and anchors; small lava tubes on either side of inlet; black coral stands; depths 65-90 feet (20-27m)
tags.wreck_cause: struck sunken rock Kalanipuao, three-quarters of a mile from shore between Koloa and Eleele
tags.wreck_cargo: 200 tons of coal and general freight
tags.wreck_note: No dedicated Wikipedia article exists for this vessel as of 2026-08-07 re-check. Vessel name, sinking date, cause, and cargo cross-confirmed 2026-08-07 across two independent Garden Island newspaper articles (2000, 2015). Build date, length, and tonnage of the vessel itself remain unconfirmed in any available source and are NOT stated as fact in the description. Captain (Walter McAllister) and crew details appear only in the 2015 article (single source) and are omitted from the site description accordingly.
tags.marine_life: Whiskered boarfish (regular), white-tip reef sharks, sea turtles, octopus, lemon butterfly fish, milletseed butterflyfish, pennant butterflyfish, helmet conch, lobsters, large crabs, black coral, dolphins (frequent)

tags.notable_features: Broad lava shelf running parallel to southeast shore, shelf starts around 60 feet then drops off with a 15-foot overhang below; pink and white cauliflower coral on shelf top; vibrant orange cup coral on overhangs; frequently done as a drift dive; strong currents possible; furthest boat site from harbor
tags.marine_life: Green sea turtles, nudibranchs (numerous species), orange-banded cowry, pincushion sea stars, Triton's trumpet shells, hermit crabs, small crustaceans in cauliflower coral, black coral on wall face
tags.depth_note: Shelf begins at 60 feet; ledge and overhang 60-100 feet (18-30m); re-confirmed 60-90ft by Seasport Divers 2026-08-07

tags.notable_features: Large arch at base of mooring festooned with orange cup coral and black coral; reef plateau at ~40 feet leads to drop-off with undercut ledges and swim-through holes; advanced due to potentially rough surface conditions and strong currents
tags.marine_life: Eels (multiple species), lobsters, longnose hawkfish (rare, confirmed), sponge crab, bicolor anthias, ghost shrimp, yellow hairy hermit crab, reef sharks
tags.depth_note: Depths 40-78 feet (12-24m); re-confirmed by Garden Isle Divers' full site list 2026-08-07
tags.source_note: Former source divessi.com (SSI MyDiveGuide) now 301-redirects to scubago.com as of 2026-08-07; same underlying listing, domain migrated

tags.notable_features: Inner and outer reef with wide channel between; outer reef offers more lava tubes and arches; coral reef comes within a few feet of low-tide shore; best May-September when north shore swells subside; dive at or near high tide
tags.marine_life: Hawksbill sea turtles, reef sharks, nudibranchs, manta rays (reported), peacock flounder, parrotfish schools, butterflyfish schools, moray eels, octopuses
tags.seasonal_note: Best May-September (calm north shore); avoid winter high surf
tags.regulatory_note: Re-checked 2026-08-07: commercial-access status is UNSETTLED and sources conflict. Seasport Divers' current site page still states trips were prohibited 'as of early 2024' and that they do not run guided trips here. Fathom Five Divers, however, currently sells bookable 'Tunnels Landing 2-Tank Shore Dive' and introductory shore-dive products at this site (May-Sept), and news coverage (Hawaii News Now, DLNR press release, April 2025) describes a small number of DOBOR commercial-use permits (reportedly 6, including Fathom Five) issued via litigation amid a broader statewide freeze on new ocean commercial permits pending environmental review. Zentacle separately describes the site as a fish-replenishment/no-entry area for several years, which conflicts with the above. Do not assert independent divers or a specific operator have unrestricted access; direct verification with DLNR/operators is required.

tags.notable_features: Multiple named sites in channel between Niihau and Lehua Crater: Vertical Awareness (pinnacle 45-300ft), Keyhole Drift to Lehua Gardens, Niihau Arches (sea caves and lava tubes), Neon Cave to Pyramid Point Drift; full-day charter (operators vary, roughly 8-12 hours including transit), certified divers only, minimum logged-dive requirement varies by operator (Seasport requires 30+ logged dives or AOW cert as of 2026-08-07 re-check; other operators cite lower minimums); visibility often hundreds of feet; strong open-ocean currents possible
tags.marine_life: Sandbar sharks, grey reef sharks (schools of 30+ reported), Hawaiian monk seals (one of highest concentrations in Hawaii), manta rays and eagle rays (seen approximately every other charter), schooling butterflyfish, bait balls, endemic Tinker's butterflyfish, endemic red lionfish, bicolor anthias, long-handed spiny lobster, spinner dolphins (November-May whales common)
tags.depth_note: Most dives 45-105 feet (14-32m); Vertical Awareness pinnacle drops to 300 feet

tags.notable_features: 11-mile sunken fringing reef off Na Pali Coast; furthest offshore dive site in Hawaii; no moorings, always live boat drift dive; first dive 60-100 feet, second dive 45-80 feet on different drop point; massive black coral stalks; ancient coral with deep cracks; surface interval exploring Na Pali sea caves
tags.marine_life: Large barracuda, spotted eagle rays, grey reef sharks, white-tip reef sharks, java moray eels, rainbow runners, stripe-belly puffers, black surgeonfish, wringtail wrasse, hammerhead sharks (reported), giant trevally, ono (wahoo), spinner dolphins (nearly guaranteed), humpback whales (winter)
tags.depth_note: First dive 60-100 feet (18-30m); second dive 45-80 feet (14-24m); re-confirmed by 2026-08-07 web search of current operator listings
tags.source_note: Former source divessi.com (SSI MyDiveGuide) now 301-redirects to scubago.com as of 2026-08-07

tags.notable_features: Protective breakwater creates calm waters; primarily documented as a boat launch/beach park for south shore and Niihau charters (May-September); facilities include restrooms, showers, picnic tables; no lifeguard. CORRECTION 2026-08-07: re-checked fathomfive.com/blog/kukuiula/ and fathomfive.com/certified-shore-dives/ directly -- neither describes Kukuiula Bay as a guided/commercial shore dive site (Fathom Five's only certified shore dives are Koloa Landing and Tunnels Beach). Prior text claiming 'Fathom Five operates guided shore dives from this site' was not supported by the source and has been removed.
tags.marine_life: No site-specific marine-life source found as of 2026-08-07 re-check. Kauai's general south-shore reef fauna (turtles, moray eels, reef fish) likely applies given the sheltered bay habitat, but no operator or forum source documents specific sightings at Kukuiula Bay itself as distinct from the harbor's role as a launch point.
tags.depth_note: Bay maximum approximately 50 feet (15m) per prior curated estimate; not independently re-confirmed by a dive-specific source in 2026-08-07 re-check

tags.notable_features: Rocky lava shore entry (booties recommended); shallow reef 3-21 feet; long swim to main reef from shore; rocky entry point; good visibility; not many fish nor much coral at main reef section
tags.marine_life: Hawaiian green sea turtles (main attraction, several often visible), whitemouth moray eels, trumpetfish, Picasso triggerfish (humuhumunukunukuapua'a), reef fish; limited coral coverage. Zentacle (re-checked 2026-08-07) also mentions scorpionfish and occasional spotted eagle rays/reef sharks, but this is single-sourced and not added to the confirmed list pending a second source.
tags.depth_note: Depths 3-21 feet (1-6m); very shallow; Zentacle's re-checked listing cites a max of 25ft, consistent within rounding
